ranking_rule: Ranked by expected DTI improvement per unit of implementation cost. 'Expected improvement' is a judgement, stated as such; only the 'status' column carries measurements, and every measured number is reproduced in evidence/*.json.

H41-A.title: NW-tip to nearest N/NNE-trace strain-transfer corridor
H41-A.layers: existing_faults.tif (catalogue geometry) + gdr_qfaults_traces.csv slip_sense; corroboration from lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif band 11 (local lineament strike)
H41-A.physical_signature: Bipartite catalogue geometry: NW-striking dextral trace endpoints connected to the nearest NNE-to-N-striking normal trace, tapered, cut at 200-300 m from the published catalogue
H41-A.why_it_should_catch_a_missing_fault: Faulds, Henry & Hinz (2005) - 'The strike-slip faults end in arrays of ~N-striking normal faults, suggesting that dextral shear diffuses into extension in the Great Basin.' Anderson & Faulds (Emerson Pass, OSTI 1110519) record the type locality INSIDE this footprint: the Pyramid Lake fault terminates and transfers strain to the Lake Range fault. If such a linkage is incompletely mapped, the corridor is exactly where the missing trace belongs.
H41-A.how_it_differs_from_prior_work: Not a catalogue-density multiplier, not a scarp filter, not a learned detector. It is a bipartite geometric construction between two kinematically distinct populations, plus an orientation test. The sibling repository 16GEMSDOE/H18-3a sourced endpoints and junctions from labels.tif as a km-scale prior; this is endpoint-specific, population-pair-specific and 100 m-resolution.
H41-A.status: MEASURED, NOT COMPETITIVE AS A STANDALONE EMISSION. On this repository's strand-level blocked holdout the corridor-only ranker earns credit_per_mass = 0.0000 (fp = mass, tp = 0) in the reference setting - i.e. essentially every corridor pixel is more than 300 m from every held-out catalogue strand. Independently, the sibling session's H41-A candidate, built with different code and a different 20 km block holdout, measured DTI = 0.0000 in all four folds (docs/downloads/holdout.json on main). TWO INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATIONS AGREE. Read together with the orientation audit (below), the correct conclusion is: the corridor is where the catalogue is NOT, which is the hypothesis, not a falsification - and a catalogue-truth holdout cannot test it either way.
H41-A.independent_test: site_control.json: see the 'Transfer-corridor hypothesis' section on validation.html. Geothermal well/spring sites are used as an instrument that does not depend on any fault catalogue.

H42.title: Basin-margin relief x 3DEP scarp x TMI field, density-packed and catalogue-thinned
H42.layers: training_features.tif band 19 (det_elev_slope), band 12 (det_elev) as the relief-position factor, band 3 (tmi_hg); data/external/lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif (USGS 3DEP scarp evidence, public); data/existing_faults.tif only as a 200 m exclusion band
H42.physical_signature: Steep terrain at LOW detrended elevation (range front / basin margin), multiplied by 1 m LiDAR scarp evidence and reduced-to-pole magnetic edge strength; greedy packing at 400 m minimum spacing, then deletion of everything within 200 m of the mapped catalogue
H42.why_it_should_catch_a_missing_fault: Great Basin geothermal systems sit on range-front faults at basin margins; a young surface-expressed scarp in that position is topographically and magnetically visible without being in the published catalogue, and the 200 m thinning removes exactly the pixels whose credit the published catalogue already expresses
H42.difference_from_prior_work: Replaces the H41 corridor geometry (measured 0.0 on the blocked holdout) and the H42 thermal-anchor weightings (measured worse than random on the SGMC instrument). Adds a relief-position factor (1 - det_elev)^1.5 that no earlier field used, and the FIRST field to beat a uniform-random control at equal mass on the 20 km blocked holdout

measured.sgmc_instrument_verdict: disagrees with the blocked holdout; recorded, not used for selection

new_candidates_ranked.layers: training_features bands 3/4/7/16/17 (tmi_hg, geod_2ndinv, geod_shearrate, ieq_n100a15, cond_surf) stacked on the shipped H42 surface
new_candidates_ranked.physical_signature: Post-hoc re-ranking of the SAME 40,000 packed locations by geophysical multi-evidence agreement, keeping geometry fixed so only ordering inside the 400 m lattice changes
new_candidates_ranked.why_missing_fault: Adds the four layers whose per-file lift is non-thermal (b03 1.02, b17 1.01, b04 0.98, b16 0.86) without moving the emission geometry that already beat both controls
new_candidates_ranked.difference: No new emission geometry, no new external data; strictly an in-place re-ranking test
new_candidates_ranked.cost: LOW (reuses scripts/holdout_h42.py with a composite score)
new_candidates_ranked.expected: small positive if the geophysical layers add independent signal; zero or negative if slope already captured it

new_candidates_ranked.layers: USGS 3DEP 1 m bare-earth DEM tiles over the footprint, curvature/slope-break at 1 m, aggregated to 100 m
new_candidates_ranked.physical_signature: Fine-scale scarp edges sub-pixel at 100 m - the resolution argument for why a real young fault can be absent from the catalogue
new_candidates_ranked.why_missing_fault: A scarp expressed at 1 m can vanish in 100 m resampling; independent fine-scale morphology is not a catalogue echo
new_candidates_ranked.difference: H42 uses the provided 100 m LiDAR scarp band; H43-B builds the predictor from 1 m tiles directly
new_candidates_ranked.cost: HIGH (tile download outside the sandbox egress allowlist; needs .github/workflows) + road/channel false-edge suppression required
new_candidates_ranked.expected: the most physically distinct untried signal; blocked by data acquisition, not by method

new_candidates_ranked.layers: GDR wellspring thermal points + the shipped H42 surface as an exclusion/ordering term
new_candidates_ranked.physical_signature: Thermal springs as surface expression of permeability along range fronts, used to RE-RANK not to generate
new_candidates_ranked.why_missing_fault: Wellsprings cluster on basin-margin faults; measured Hot+Warm 4,118 with 3,415 more than 300 m from any mapped fault
new_candidates_ranked.difference: Thermal was anti-informative as a density generator (lift 0.05) but was never tested as an in-place ordering term on an already-validated geometry
new_candidates_ranked.expected: uncertain; one fold-consistent re-ranking run decides it
new_candidates_ranked.risk: 27,092 rows are one feature across several layer rows (dedupe on name,row,col,temp) and classes include the trailing-space 'Hot ' value

new_candidates_ranked.layers: catalogue-distance thinning sweep on the shipped H42 field (1, 2, 3, 4 px)
new_candidates_ranked.physical_signature: The exact mechanism that produced the 0.2778 report, applied as a controlled sweep instead of a single setting
new_candidates_ranked.why_missing_fault: Not a new detector: a precision/recall trade on the emission boundary, which the ledger shows is worth +0.00487 on the archived base
new_candidates_ranked.difference: H33-2-B2 applied 2 px once; this measures the response curve on the new geometry
new_candidates_ranked.expected: +0.001 to +0.005 if the archived thinning response transfers

new_candidates_ranked.layers: 2020 M>=4 seismicity envelope (16 events, azimuth 101 deg, half-axis 11.7 km) as an ordering term
new_candidates_ranked.physical_signature: Coulomb-stress/aftershock envelope favourable to fluid flow - a time-dependent signal no static layer contains
new_candidates_ranked.why_missing_fault: A fault that ruptured or was stressed in 2020 need not be in a compilation that stops earlier; the envelope is independent of the catalogue
new_candidates_ranked.difference: Seismicity was only ever used as context; it has never entered a surface
new_candidates_ranked.cost: LOW but the sample is 16 events, none within 300 m of a mapped fault
new_candidates_ranked.expected: small; ranking risk high (a 16-event sample cannot define a regional envelope)

validation_policy: A candidate is only slot-eligible if it is emitted fresh inside every held-out 20 km block, competes at equal mass, and beats both the uniform-random and training-density controls in all four folds (gems41 metric.dti, eroded interiors).

Report every instrument's reading, including the ones that disagree with the selection. The SGMC independent-map instrument over-rewards mass and high terrain; it is published, never used as the selector.
Never tune on the 0.2778 figure; it is user-reported with no organizer receipt.
The blocked holdout's truth is the published catalogue and cannot reward a genuinely new fault - state that limitation wherever a holdout number appears.
